# Gleb Rosev — Founding Engineer, AI Agents @ YAGNI (yagni.app)

Gleb Rosev (also spelled Rossev) is a Founding Engineer at YAGNI (yagni.app) in Tbilisi, building production AI agent teams; previously Staff Harness Engineer at Sully.ai; 8+ years in engineering; medical degree.

> Making AI agents dependable in production, not just impressive in a demo.

- **Current Role**: Founding Engineer, AI Agents at YAGNI (yagni.app) (`https://yagni.app`) — Nov 2026 — Present (core team, working with the founders)
- **Location**: Tbilisi, Georgia
- **Experience**: 8+ years building production software systems, leading teams of 5–12 engineers
- **Email**: rossevgleb@gmail.com

## Executive Summary
I build software systems where reliability matters, and I make AI agent teams dependable in production, not just impressive in a demo. Now: Founding Engineer at YAGNI (yagni.app), working with the founders on AI agent teams (PM, Builder, Reviewer) that take work from a proposal to a merged GitHub PR under human-approved plans. Before that: Staff Harness Engineer on healthcare voice AI at Sully.ai. 8+ years across full-stack, mobile, cloud and engineering management, plus a medical degree.

How I work: I build with AI agents every day — I plan, delegate to agents, review their output with a second "judge" agent, and keep the human decision where it matters.

## Career Experience (Synchronized with src/data/profile.ts)

### YAGNI (yagni.app) (Nov 2026 — Present) — Founding Engineer, AI Agents
*Location*: Tbilisi, Georgia · Remote | *Focus*: Founding Team · Agent Benchmarks · Multi-Tenant Isolation · Self-Healing Syncs
Early-stage US startup building named AI agent teams that take engineering work from proposal to merged GitHub pull request under human-approved plans.
- Tenant isolation: tenant-scoped query guards and sandboxed code execution.
- Connector backfills made self-healing: stuck-cursor recovery, progress tracking and hard caps for long syncs of large workspaces.
- Code-review agent reliability: fixed ticket-key collisions between YAGNI and external trackers that sent the reviewer to the wrong issue.
- Agent benchmarks: realistic engineering task suites that show whether a prompt, model or harness change makes agents better or worse.
- Risk radar: flags stalled customer runs before the customer reports them.
- Self-improving loop (experimental): a meta-agent reads failed runs, isolates the cause and drafts a fix for the team to review.
- Monorepo build chain reduced to one command for fresh checkouts, worktrees and CI.
- Technical point of contact for pilot customers: demos, debugging live runs, turning feedback into engineering work.

### Sully.ai (Sep 2025 — Oct 2026) — Staff Harness Engineer, AI Voice Systems
*Location*: Dubai, UAE | *Focus*: 15s → 0s Dead Air at Pickup · MENA Launch · Real-Time Voice AI
AI receptionist platform for healthcare: voice and text agents for scheduling, care coordination and clinic operations. Sully.ai serves 400+ healthcare organizations.
- Led core engineering for the MENA launch: UAE infrastructure, Azure Blob Storage support, regional configuration and production readiness.
- Removed ~15 s of dead air at pickup on outbound calls: the agent was greeting the caller while the line was still ringing.
- Made agent dispatch reliable on LiveKit: retry-and-verify, no more duplicate agents in one call, no more silent calls.
- Designed UAE audio-residency guardrails so TTS and STT fallbacks stay within approved regional providers instead of silently routing elsewhere.
- Built patient-data validation for outbound campaigns: local phone formats, customer-specific schemas, clinic rules.
- Built high-volume stress testing with headless LiveKit participants, Loki and Mimir validation, and runtime health checks; found and fixed the memory cascade behind burst failures.

### Kingpin (Sep 2024 — Sep 2025) — Engineering Manager / Senior Full-Stack
*Location*: Dubai, UAE | *Focus*: 12 Engineers Led · -80% Feedback Analysis Time · Canary Releases
AI-powered multi-tenant B2B SaaS platform for wholesale.
- Led a cross-functional team of up to 12 people while staying active in architecture and code.
- Delivered multi-tenant catalog/order workflows with ERP/CRM syncs and feature-flagged trunk-based releases.
- Built an LLM feedback pipeline converting Sales/CS input into product insights (-80% analysis time).

### Kernelics (Feb 2023 — Sep 2024) — Lead React Native Developer
*Location*: London, UK | *Focus*: 100K+ Downloads · 5 Engineers Led · Unified Monorepo
Product engineering across fintech, crypto, AI & healthcare.
- Led a 5-person team across web and mobile product delivery in a shared monorepo.
- Integrated native cryptographic modules into a flagship application with 100,000+ downloads.
- Hardened CI/CD build pipelines and production runtime stability.

### BattlePro & ITechArt (Jan 2018 — Feb 2023) — Frontend Team Lead · RN Manager · Full-Stack
*Location*: New York & New Jersey, US | *Focus*: 220ms TTFB (25→55 SP) · $10M+ Raised Arch · 1,500+ Students/Yr
Sports tournament platform, full-stack cloud architectures & technical mentorship.
- Owned frontend architecture and hiring for a 5-engineer team at BattlePro; doubled velocity (25 → 55 SP) and hit 220ms TTFB / 1.7s TTI.
- Architected a full-stack virtual networking platform at ITechArt that subsequently attracted $10M+ in investment.
- Delivered 150+ advanced React/JS lectures at TeachMeSkills; curriculum adopted by 1,500+ students/year.

## Writing (full posts on rossev.dev, each with a 30-second brief; most also on LinkedIn)
- [One AI Agent PR Costs $82 on Opus and $13 on Open-Weight Models](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-agent-pr-token-cost-gap/) (2026-11-04): Count the real token cost per PR, because on live features it can be 10 to 100 times the cost of small tickets.
- [I Refused to Pay the Hacker Who Found Our Signup Hole](https://rossev.dev/writing/unpaid-extortion-exposed-signup-flaw/) (2026-11-03): Protect signup flows from mass abuse before a stranger's extortion email forces you to.
- [Before Letting a Model Rewrite Your Harness, Read Your Logs](https://rossev.dev/writing/read-logs-before-rewriting-harness/) (2026-11-02): Fix the environment and code bugs your logs reveal before letting a model tune your prompts.
- [A Model's Output Is a Claim, Not Trusted Input](https://rossev.dev/writing/model-output-is-a-claim/) (2026-10-30): Treat model output and agent memory as claims that a deterministic check or a person must approve before they enter your system.
- [Context Selection Matters More Than Context Size for Agents](https://rossev.dev/writing/context-selection-beats-context-size/) (2026-10-29): Show the agent only what changes its next decision, instead of adding more context when it fails.
- [Unstable AI Agents Need Contracts, Not Longer Prompts](https://rossev.dev/writing/agent-stability-comes-from-contracts-not-prompts/) (2026-10-28): Enforce agent behavior at the interface with typed tool specs, isolated context, and structured errors instead of adding prompt text.
- [Single-Turn Benchmarks Reward Guessing, Not Agent Work](https://rossev.dev/writing/single-turn-evals-miss-agent-failures/) (2026-10-27): For agents, grade whether the task got done across the whole loop, not the first reply alone.
- [Bargaining Over Estimates Shrinks the Buffer, Not the Work](https://rossev.dev/writing/bargaining-estimates-shrinks-buffer/) (2026-10-26): When a number needs to come down, cut scope instead of negotiating the estimate.
- [Silence in an Architecture Review Is a Warning Sign](https://rossev.dev/writing/silence-in-design-review-is-risk/) (2026-10-19): Treat a quiet design review as a risk signal and push for real debate before the build starts.
- [Overpromising Might Be an Underrated Management Skill](https://rossev.dev/writing/overpromising-rewarded-over-realism/) (2026-10-15): Judge managers by what they delivered against what they promised, not by how exciting their next plan sounds.
- [A Super-Productive Employee Is a Single Point of Failure](https://rossev.dev/writing/super-productive-employee-single-point-failure/) (2026-09-10): Build a team that can survive losing any one person instead of betting the budget on a single rockstar.
- [Positive Feedback Is Information: It Tells You the Bar](https://rossev.dev/writing/positive-feedback-sets-the-bar-to-optimize/) (2026-07-17): Give specific examples of valuable work instead of vague principles, so people know the bar and can repeat it efficiently.
- [Stop Using AI Only to Write Code: Connect It to Your Whole Environment](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-as-engineering-context-interface/) (2026-07-14): Connect your AI agent to the tools where context lives, so it can work on real tasks instead of isolated code snippets.
- [The Biggest AI Bottleneck Is the Last Mile, Not the Technology](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-last-mile-is-human-adoption/) (2026-07-09): Treat adoption as a core engineering problem: earn trust and fit into existing workflows, not just improve the model.
- [I Showed Up to the Wrong Event a Week Early and Met Great People](https://rossev.dev/writing/wrong-date-led-to-good-evening/) (2026-07-07): When a plan breaks, pick the next good option instead of going home, and you may gain more than you lost.
- [Engineering Has Shifted From Choosing Tools to Asking the Right Questions](https://rossev.dev/writing/engineering-center-of-gravity-shifted/) (2026-07-03): When AI takes over routine technical choices, put your effort into users, evaluation, and whether you are solving the right problem.
- [A Tiny AI Voice Bug Can Cost More Trust Than a Major Outage](https://rossev.dev/writing/small-ai-bugs-destroy-trust/) (2026-07-02): Treat small, user-visible details as real quality defects, because users judge trust by what they notice, not by your internal metrics.
- [Problems Are Cheap. Decisions Are What Companies Pay For](https://rossev.dev/writing/turn-problems-into-decisions/) (2026-06-13): Turn every problem you raise into a concrete decision with options, so the room knows what to do next.
- [Complaining vs Escalating: Make the Trade-off Visible](https://rossev.dev/writing/escalate-with-options-not-complaints/) (2026-06-13): When you escalate, name the concrete trade-off and the consequence of not acting, so the manager can choose.
- [Silence Is Agreement: Speak Up About Constraints Early](https://rossev.dev/writing/silence-is-agreement-speak-early/) (2026-06-13): Name your constraints (time, priorities, missing information) as soon as you see them, because silence will be read as a yes.
- [Your Job as an Engineer Is Not to Defend the Plan](https://rossev.dev/writing/explain-the-cost-not-defend-the-plan/) (2026-06-08): When new work arrives, ask what it displaces and make that cost visible so the business can decide.
- [Estimates Are Hypotheses, Not Promises](https://rossev.dev/writing/estimates-are-hypotheses-not-promises/) (2026-06-08): State the assumptions behind an estimate out loud so a changed assumption moves the date instead of breaking a promise.
- [Design Patterns Are the Language You Use to Direct AI](https://rossev.dev/writing/patterns-are-the-language-for-ai-orchestration/) (2026-06-03): Name the patterns you want (SOLID, DDD) instead of describing vague goals, so you and the AI can talk about concrete, well-known things.
- [AI Will Replace Routine Work, Not Responsibility](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-replaces-routine-not-responsibility/) (2026-06-01): Use AI for routine tasks like CRUD and JSON transforms, and keep ownership of the result yourself.
- [Pressure Does Not Make Engineering Faster](https://rossev.dev/writing/pressure-does-not-speed-up-engineering/) (2026-04-19): Real speed comes from understanding constraints and protecting quality, not from pushing the team harder.
- [Approval Process Can Cost More Than the Tool It Protects](https://rossev.dev/writing/approval-process-costs-more-than-tool/) (2026-04-13): Compare the cost of the approval process with the cost of the thing being approved, and simplify purchases that cost less to buy than to review.
- [Cursor Works as a Planning Hub for Epics and Tasks](https://rossev.dev/writing/cursor-as-planning-hub-for-epics/) (2025-09-16): Use an AI coding assistant to turn scattered business notes into a structured epic and task files before you move them into your tracker.
- [Fix the System Before Buying More AI Tools](https://rossev.dev/writing/docops-ai-workflows-over-tools/) (2025-09-12): Build repeatable documentation-driven workflows so AI handles routine steps and people handle decisions.
- [Hands-On Hiring: Why Delegating Interviews Costs You Good Engineers](https://rossev.dev/writing/hiring-managers-should-do-interviews-personally/) (2025-09-08): As a hiring manager, run the key hiring stages yourself instead of delegating them to others.
- [Feed AI Assistants Documentation First, Not Clever Prompts](https://rossev.dev/writing/documentation-first-ai-development-crewai/) (2025-09-03): Write product, functional and architecture specs before asking an AI assistant to generate code, then version each release.
- [Four CrewAI Agents Turn a One-Line Prompt Into a D&D Monster](https://rossev.dev/writing/crewai-agents-generate-dnd-monsters/) (2025-09-02): Split a complex generation task across specialized agents with clear roles instead of cramming everything into one prompt.
- [Stop Chatting With AI and Build Repeatable Workflows](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-workflow-human-validator/) (2025-08-30): Build AI workflows with a fixed source, clear requirements, and a human validator before anything is published.
- [AI Operator or Architect: Which Side Will You Take?](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-operator-vs-architect-frontend/) (2025-08-25): Use AI for small tasks but keep the system picture yourself, especially in frontend where UX judgment stays human.
- [I Skipped Three.js for My Hero Scene. A WebGL Dev Found the Bug in One Sentence.](https://rossev.dev/writing/no-threejs-topology/) (2026-11-04): Per-frame animation runs twice as fast at 120 Hz; easing needs 1 − (1 − rate)^frames, not rate × dt.
- [My Logo Heals Itself. Then I Erased It Into a Stick.](https://rossev.dev/writing/self-healing-monogram/) (2026-11-04): A local model can’t recover information that isn’t there: give it a dumb global supervisor that knows when to restart.
- [RimWorld Is a Better Engineering Management Simulator Than You Think](https://rossev.dev/writing/engineering-management-systems-thinking/) (2026-10-13): Design a system where people make good decisions without you, instead of overriding their queues every 30 seconds.
- [Every Engineering Estimate Hides Two Different Numbers](https://rossev.dev/writing/every-engineering-estimate-is-two-things/) (2026-10-19): Ask for the one unknown that could blow up the estimate and test it early, instead of arguing about a single date.
- [The New AI Bottleneck Isn’t Generation — It’s Verification](https://rossev.dev/writing/the-new-ai-bottleneck/) (2026-10-19): Harnesses, automated evals, and runtime observability separate AI toys from production.
- [AI Agents Wrote More Code, But the Bottleneck Moved to Review](https://rossev.dev/writing/ai-agents-30-percent-more-code/) (2026-10-23): Measure cycle time and review capacity after adopting AI coding tools, not just code volume.
- [AI Security Tools Need to Work When the Incident Is Messy](https://rossev.dev/writing/attackers-kept-attacking-opencode/) (2026-10-23): Test AI security tools in messy incident conditions, not only in demos.
- [The Junior-Senior Gap Is Now Product Judgment, Not Syntax](https://rossev.dev/writing/technical-seniority-is-dead/) (2026-10-18): Evaluate seniors on whether they know what not to build, not on framework trivia.
- [Don't Use an LLM Where an If/Else Will Do](https://rossev.dev/writing/god-damn-5k-if-else/) (2026-10-19): Write deterministic code first and bring in an agent only for the part of the problem that rules and state machines cannot handle.
- [Stop Using LLMs as the World's Most Expensive If-Statements](https://rossev.dev/writing/stop-using-llms-as-expensive-regex/) (2026-10-16): Use specialized non-generative models for routing, classification, signal cleaning and tracking, and keep the LLM for tasks that need text.
- [Explanations Describe Failure, Ownership Changes the Plan](https://rossev.dev/writing/explanation-vs-ownership/) (2026-06-13): After a failure, pair every explanation with a concrete decision or revised plan.
